# 4 Ezra Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Ezra restores the scriptures

---

**1** On the third day, while I was sitting under an oak tree, a voice called out from a bush in front of me: Ezra! Ezra!

**2** I said: Here I am, Lord. And I stood up.

**3** He said: In a bush I once revealed myself to Moses and spoke to him when my people were enslaved in Egypt.

**4** I sent him and brought my people out of Egypt, and led him up to Mount Sinai, where I kept him close to me for many days.

**5** I told him astonishing things, showed him the hidden secrets of the ages and the end of all seasons, and gave him this command:

**6** Some of these words you will publish openly; others you will keep hidden.

**7** And now I give you the same instruction.

**8** Hold in your heart all the signs I have shown you, all the dreams you have seen, and all the interpretations you have heard.

**9** For you are going to be taken up from among human beings, and from this point on you will remain with my son and with those like you, until the times reach their end.

**10** For the world has spent its youth, and the times are growing old.

**11** The age has been divided into twelve parts, and nine of them have already gone by,

**12** along with half of the tenth — leaving two parts after the midpoint of the tenth.

**13** So put your affairs in order. Rebuke your people. Comfort those who are crushed. Give up what is corruptible.

**14** Let go of mortal concerns. Lay down everything that weighs a human being down. Strip off your weak and fragile nature.

**15** Release your most tormenting thoughts and hurry to get free from these times.

**16** Because what is coming will be worse than anything you have yet seen.

**17** Look at how those who grow old weaken: the older they get, the further they drift from truth.

**18** You think wisdom will come with age, but the more you age the more your understanding fails.

**19** The world is already in decline.

**20** I answered: Lord, may I say something?

**21** I will go as you command and rebuke the people of this generation. But who will guide those born after us?

**22** The world is in darkness, and its inhabitants have no light.

**23** Your law was burned. No one knows what you have done, or what you will do.

**24** If I have found any favor with you, breathe your Holy Spirit into me, and I will write down everything that has happened from the beginning of the world — all that was written in your law — so that people can find the way, and those who want to live in the last days will know how to live.

**25** He answered: Go and assemble the people and tell them not to look for you for forty days.

**26** Prepare a large supply of writing tablets from boxwood. Take five men with you — Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Ethan, and Asiel — who can write fast.

**27** Come back here, and I will light within your heart the lamp of understanding that will not go out until you have finished writing everything I give you.

**28** When you are done, you will make some things public and deliver others quietly to the wise. Begin writing tomorrow at this time.

**29** I went as he commanded, gathered the entire people, and said:

**30** Listen, Israel.

**31** Our ancestors began as refugees in Egypt. They were set free,

**32** given the law of life — which they did not keep — which you also, following in their footsteps, have broken.

**33** You were given the land of Zion as your inheritance. But you and your fathers acted wickedly and did not walk in the ways the Most High commanded.

**34** Because he is a just judge, in due time he took back from you what he had given you.

**35** Now you are here, and your kinspeople are far away.

**36** But if you will take control of your own understanding and discipline your hearts, you will be kept alive, and after death you will receive mercy.

**37** For after death comes judgment, when we will live again; and at that time the names of the righteous will come to light and the actions of the wicked will be exposed.

**38** So now, let no one come to me or look for me for forty days.

**39** I took the five men as instructed, and we went out to the field and stayed there.

**40** The next day a voice called out: Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I am about to give you.

**41** I opened my mouth — and a full cup was held out to me, filled with something that looked like water but had the color of fire.

**42** I took it and drank. As soon as I drank it, understanding poured out from my heart and wisdom swelled in my chest — my spirit was holding on to everything it had been given.

**43** My mouth was opened and it did not close again.

**44** The Most High also gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote down, in turn, everything I dictated, in a script they did not know.

**45** For forty days they wrote. During the day they wrote; at night they ate.

**46** As for me, I spoke all day and through the night I did not stop.

**47** In the forty days, ninety-four books were written.

**48** When the forty days were over, the Most High spoke: Now publish the first twenty-four that you wrote, so that those who are worthy and those who are not may both read them.

**49** But keep the last seventy back, and hand them over only to those who are truly wise among your people.

**50** For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.
